one_month.note: The exact production-context AI replay uses the frozen research mean injected by the live runtime.

historical_options_replay.method: Historical option trade bars were used for price/liquidity proxies. Arbitrary-past snapshot BBO and Greeks are not exposed by Alpaca's snapshot endpoint, so no exact historical live-constructor fill claim is made.
historical_options_replay.finding: Correct underlying direction does not guarantee a one-hour debit-spread profit; spread expression and short-leg liquidity materially affect realized outcomes.

constructor_defect_and_fix.defect: Maximizing net-delta-per-debit could select extremely far-OTM near-zero-delta shorts that looked efficient mathematically but had weak historical trade-print coverage.
constructor_defect_and_fix.red_regression: A valid 0.02-absolute-delta short beat a 0.15-delta short under the old ranking for both calls and puts.

rejected_changes.opening_sign_reversion_guard: rejected; materially worsened the quarter and would have blocked the correct Sep 1 reversion
rejected_changes.rolling_five_signal_regime_gate: not promoted; retrospective improvement was not robust enough and it would have blocked correct August/Sep 1 reversions
rejected_changes.hard_10pct_spot_width_cap: rejected; removed too many otherwise valid recent candidates
rejected_changes.ai_prompt_or_model_change: rejected; repeated historical contexts produced zero action flips and six-month AI replay outperformed raw continuation

limitations: AI uses the current deployed model/prompt on historical timestamp-capped Alpaca context; this is current-policy replay, not a recreation of the provider implementation that existed on each historical date.
Historical option bars are trade-based and cannot reconstruct arbitrary-past snapshot bid/ask and Greeks used by the live constructor.
Historical option trade-print coverage is a liquidity proxy, not proof of executable historical BBO fillability.
Directional-return sums are diagnostic, not compounded account returns or exact option P&L.
